# Judging visual work

Judge rendered work from what renders, not from a passing build or a report's claims.

## Pick the platform skill

1. Pick the platform design skill for the work before the first Worker.visual or Reviewer.visual dispatch: `web-design`, `mobile-design`, `desktop-design` or `tui-design`, one for each platform of a multi-platform project.
2. Name each skill's file in the criteria of both specialists by its literal absolute path, `guidance/<family>/<name>/SKILL.md` under the package folder (as the dispatch rules say), with a blocking criterion to read it and to build and inspect (Worker.visual) or judge (Reviewer.visual) against its checklist and capture list.
3. Start the render target first, per platform (the `dev-server` skill).

The platform skill is the only design guidance the two specialists get: the shared core (direction before code, the plan, copy, the quality floor), the platform rules, the refuse list and the capture checklist.

## Accept

Your own final pass, after Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual, decides acceptance:

1. Read the final captures Reviewer.visual lists, at each size and variant the criteria and the skill's capture checklist name, against that skill's checklist (read its file), and accept only when they pass.
2. Treat Reviewer.visual's observations (viewport, interaction and visible result for each) as input to the decision, not as the decision. A Worker.visual report alone, or an inspection reported as blocked, accepts nothing.
3. Keep the pass to those final captures: open none from an earlier round and take none yourself. For a missing size or variant, or a web page that Reviewer.visual inspected live and for which Worker.visual saved no captures, have Worker.visual or Worker.operations save the final captures at the listed sizes and variants, which Reviewer.visual then lists. Judge nothing you cannot see.
4. A material finding of your pass starts a repair like any other, whether or not the reviewer reported it; say in the final report when your pass overruled the reviewer.

Read an image in the main thread only to show it to the user (a path is not delivery) or to settle a concrete doubt about that evidence, besides the final pass; Reviewer.visual and Worker.visual hand over captures and paths so that you do not have to.

## Material discrepancies

A discrepancy is material, and starts a repair whatever its size, when it affects any of these: acceptance; hierarchy or composition; legibility (cramped, overlapping, clipped or disappearing text); responsiveness at a viewport or size the criteria list; whether text and numbers state the content correctly (a title that misstates what it covers); accessibility; interaction correctness; adherence to a reference; obvious production quality. Unnecessary text, headings, cards or badges are design defects. Only pure preference, with none of these effects, stays unrepaired: list it apart, marked optional.

A departure from the platform skill's direction rules that has none of these effects is preference too. The project's design system and the user's explicit requirements outrank taste.

## Repair

1. Repair a material finding without asking when the repair keeps the user's requirements and needs no choice between fixes; otherwise ask through `ask_user_question` with a recommended default.
2. Dispatch Worker.visual with the findings as criteria and say "round N of 3" in the brief, then Reviewer.visual to re-inspect only what the repair touched, until the inspection is clean; then repeat your final pass on the captures that changed.
3. Allow at most three rounds per finding, counted across Worker.visual dispatches; after three, report the finding as a blocker.
4. Name each skipped preference in the final report, without a fix.

## Explanatory pages

When a visual explanation or chart carries what prose cannot, build one self-contained HTML page. Such a page illustrates and does not validate a software interface. T3 Code's `html_preview` and `html_render` are optional aids, available only when T3 Code's tools are enabled: `html_preview` returns a PNG with console output so you can check the page first, and `html_render` shows the finished page inline in the reply. Without them, save the page as a file, check it as far as the environment allows and give the user its path, naming what you could not check.

## Iteration evidence

Before any task source edits, dispatch a qualified specialist to collect and preserve the immutable original revision, visual evidence and conditions. After the root creates each source commit, dispatch an appropriate existing visual or operations specialist to collect evidence without source edits on that actual commit before independent review, acceptance or push. Compare it with both the original baseline and the immediately previous commit: for the first commit the previous revision is the original; advance the previous revision after each commit and never overwrite the original. Use screenshots and real interaction, plus video when the host supports it. Record revisions, evidence paths and conditions; exploratory precommit checks do not substitute for committed evidence. Mark unavailable comparisons Unknown with a concrete reason and a blocker when the requested target requires them; never substitute the last PR for the original baseline.

Associate reports and artifacts with the commit SHA outside the source commit as needed, and point persisted state and handoff to them. Do not create recursive evidence-only commits. Use this evidence in review and acceptance alongside the final captures.
